Exercise 1. Write the fitness function for a genetic algorithm aimed at solving the Sudoku puzzle.
A Sudoku puzzle consists of a 9x9 grid, in which each cell must contain a number between 1 and 9, 
according to the following rules:
• Each row must contain exactly one instance of each number (no repetitions on rows)
• Each column must contain exactly one instance of each number (no repetitions on columns)
• The grid is divided in 9 3x3 sub-grids: each sub-grid must contain exactly one instance of 
each number (no repetitions on sub-grids)
You can assume that the input to the function is given in the form of a matrix indexed as:
individual[row][column]
in which each cell contains a number between 1 and 9.

Exercise 2. Write the fitness function for a genetic algorithm aimed at solving the Knapsack 
problem. In the Knapsack problem you are tasked with the goal of filling a knapsack (having 
maximum capacity) with items from a list, maximizing the total value of the knapsack but without 
exceeding the capacity. There is a single copy of each item and each item has a weight and value.
You can assume that the input to the function is given in the form of:
• A maximum weight (integer) capacity
• An array of weights, indexed as weights[i]
• An array of values, indexed as values[i]
• A binary (0/1) array specifying which items are in the knapsack, indexed as individual[i]
